description: Scenario tests for the voice-builder skill. A run passes only when every item in 'expect' is satisfied. Written before the skill body (test-first).

evals.name: happy-path-good-samples
evals.input: Build my voice. Here are 6 of my best LinkedIn posts: [samples].
expect: reads brand-profile first if available
analyzes across the six layers (lexicon, syntax, rhetoric, structure, stance, negative space)
cites evidence (quotes from the samples) for the patterns it names
distills a 5-7 signature fingerprint plus a 'never' list
writes a voice.md following the template (operational rules, not adjectives)
runs the voice test: generates a post on a NEW topic and scores it against the fingerprint
shows the user the test post and what it changed

evals.name: no-samples-route-to-interview
evals.context: The user has provided no writing samples.
expect: does NOT fabricate a voice from nothing
asks for samples, suggesting the easiest sources (incl. a spoken transcript/voice memo)
offers to fall back to brand-profile's voice interview if no samples exist
does not produce a confident voice.md without evidence

evals.name: thin-samples-low-confidence
evals.input: Here's one short post I wrote. Build my voice from this.
expect: extracts what is observable from the limited sample
marks the voice.md confidence as low and names which layers are uncertain
asks for more samples (especially a spoken transcript) to raise confidence
does not overstate certainty

evals.name: inconsistent-samples-voice-drift
evals.input: Here are my samples — some formal newsletters and some loose, funny tweets.
expect: does NOT average the conflicting samples into a bland middle
flags the inconsistency explicitly
asks which represents the target voice, or captures the split as channel-based tone variation
anchors the fingerprint on the target voice

evals.name: aspirational-voice
evals.input: I write pretty dry corporate stuff now, but I want to sound bold and punchy like [creator].
expect: separates current voice from target voice
collects or analyzes aspirational references and labels them as aspirational
is transparent about what is being borrowed vs. native
produces a target voice.md that is still ownable, not an impersonation

evals.name: multiple-voices-no-blend
evals.input: Set up voice for our brand account and separately for our founder's personal account.
expect: creates a separate voice.md per voice, clearly named
never blends the two voices together
notes anything genuinely shared vs distinct

evals.name: validation-loop-enforced
evals.input: Here are my samples — just give me the voice.md, skip the testing.
expect: still runs at least one generate-and-score validation pass
explains briefly why an untested voice guide is unreliable
delivers the voice.md only after showing it can produce an on-voice post

evals.name: exclude-bad-samples
evals.input: Here are some samples — a couple are our legal/boilerplate website copy and one was written by an agency.
expect: excludes ghostwritten, boilerplate, and committee-edited samples
explains why those don't represent the person's voice
builds the voice only from genuine first-person samples
